work.name: NVIDIA
highlights: Learned formal verification basics, including SystemVerilog assertions, assumes and covers.
Verified FSM and credit-valid VIPs; found bugs in the FSM VIP and fixed them.

Automated root cause analysis of cover failures (which, unlike assertion failures, give no traces) using a staircase approach, ~30% more accurate than an off-the-shelf LLM baseline on a synthetic benchmark.

work.name: SAFARI Research Group, ETH Zurich
work.summary: Memory and storage architectures, DRAM simulation
highlights: Explored memory and storage architectures such as DRAM and SSD, and interconnects like Compute Express Link.
Worked on adding GDDR7 support to Ramulator 2.1 (open-source DRAM simulator): read-clock (RCKSTRT/RCKSTOP) modes, PAM3/NRZ signalling, and device-timing, scheduling and multi-channel tests.

work.name: Quintrans Hyperloop
highlights: Developed a control strategy for Active Electromagnetic Suspension (EMS) using a PID controller for levitation.
Implemented a Gain Scheduling control scheme to handle nonlinear dynamics and variable load in the EMS.
Designed a current limiter circuit using the ADG1222 analog switch to improve hardware safety and protection.

projects.name: PuMSolve: Solver-Aided Discovery of DRAM-Resident Compute Kernels
projects.summary: A Z3-based framework that synthesizes in-DRAM programs for a target operation, or proves that none exists (solo project)
highlights: Finds the minimal mechanism set a kernel requires and proves impossibility for all program lengths (e.g. XOR is unreachable under monotone-only mechanisms).
All 100 kernels in a Boolean evaluation agree with the monotonicity theorem, and a full adder is verified up to 32 bits (model-level results).
